binders: A sequence of integers n tending to infinity.
A sequence of connection probabilities p=p(n) in [0,1].
Random graphs G_n distributed as G(n,p(n)).
Positive constants c_- and c_+ independent of n.
hypotheses: For all sufficiently large n, c_- ≤ d_n ≤ c_+; equivalently, the expected-degree sequence is bounded above and bounded away from zero, d_n=Θ(1).
conclusions: There is a constant c>0 and a threshold N such that, for every n≥N, the probability that G_n has a vertex of degree at least c log n/log log n is at least 0.9.
definitions_and_conventions: In G(n,p), every unordered pair of distinct vertices is connected independently with probability p.
The degree of a vertex is the number of incident edges.
The notation Ω(log n/log log n) denotes a lower bound by a positive constant multiple of log n/log log n for all sufficiently large n.
The correction replaces the printed upper-bound-only condition d=O(1) by the nondegenerate very-sparse regime d=Θ(1).
implicit_context: The asymptotic variable is the graph size n.
The probability is over the independent random edges of G_n.
The connection probability p may depend on n.
The base of the logarithm does not affect the asserted asymptotic order.

undebatable_constraints: The graph model must be G(n,p) with independent edges and expected degree d=(n−1)p.

ambiguities.impact: The explicit fixed-threshold reading requires eventual probability at least 0.9; a probability tending to one is a stronger possible reading.

conclusions: The probability that G_n contains any edge is at most n(n−1)p_n/2 and therefore tends to zero.

contracts.contract_plain_english: The printed condition allows the expected degree to vanish. For example, with p(n)=n^−3 the expected degree is O(1), but the graph has no edges with probability tending to one. Its maximum degree is therefore zero with high probability, so no positive multiple of log n/log log n can be attained with probability 0.9. This obstructs the literal statement and explains the need for a positive lower bound on d.
